title: Why the Jensen Huang rally faded so quickly
summary: Market Hang tackles the top stories of the day. Including why Monday's Jensen Huang rally faded within a day, what teeth the congressional hearings and board investigation can have given why he was reinstated, and whether the market is sniffing out a peak in the AI CapEx cycle the way it has in past build-outs. The panel debates what the VIX and implied correlations say about last week's selloff, why small caps lagged even in the rally, how a Fed rate hike changes the cost of capital for data center projects, and why investors now have to "take out the pencil" and discount AI earnings years out, before closing with a lighter debate on whether anyone would watch the Super Bowl in an IMAX theater.

title: Stocks give back gains as Anthropic dips below IPO price
summary:
Hosts Julie Hyman and Jake Conley, joined on the couch by Barron's markets reporter Jacob Sonenshine, tackle the top stories of the day. Including futures sliding after Monday's biggest rally since April 2025, Anthropic briefly trading below its $83 IPO price, a Wall Street Journal report that the U.S. is preparing new tariffs on China and dozens of other countries, and whether Jensen Huang's return leaves Nvidia owing a favor to the White House.

The team is joined by Seaport Research Partners senior analyst Jay Goldberg and Creative Strategies CEO and principal analyst Ben Bajarin to discuss what Jensen Huang needs to tell shareholders, the competitive threat from Broadcom and AMD, and whether Nvidia's financing of neoclouds is a wobbly foundation. The show closes on Strategy trading below the value of its Bitcoin, Sanofi's $41 billion deal for Insmed, and a strong day for retail earnings from Best Buy, Dollar Tree, Dick's, Abercrombie, and Kohl's.

title: Who is holding Jensen Huang accountable? It sure looks like nobody
summary: Sozzi Unleashed host Brian Sozzi digs into day two of Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia. Including a Financial Times report that interim CEO Colette Kress was left out of the talks to bring Huang back, a Wall Street Journal report that Huang disclosed more affairs to the board than previously known, why Brian says Nvidia is effectively a "board of one," and what history says about returning founders from Steve Jobs and Howard Schultz to Kevin Plank.
